output.summary: A deciduous cherry tree native to Izu Ōshima and the Izu Peninsula on Honshū near Tokyo, Japan, the Oshima cherry is grown for its ornamental blossoms. In spring, it bears clusters of five-petalled white flowers with gold stamens, as well as small black cherries.
output.edibilityNote: Its fruit is edible; dried flowers make tea, and leaves are used in cooking, though P. speciosa is not the only sakura leaf used.
